highest_reported.source: Chung, Du, and Wesley, Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment, arXiv:2608.23691v2, Section 6.1, Theorem 2.1.
highest_reported.reproduction_status: The paper gives an explicit infinite family for p=3 mod 4 and an exact size formula. This task specializes the published line construction to p=31, reconstructs all 993 line witnesses, and exactly recomputes 8,289 union points. The source also links a first-party verification notebook and Lean proof. This is a feasible construction, not a proof of finite optimality.

best_human.source: Bukh and Chao, Sharp density bounds on the finite field Kakeya problem, 2021, Section 4; https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00074
best_human.provenance: Traditional quadratic-residue construction: the odd-field almost-Kakeya set of size 31*((31+1)/2)^2, united with the full plane t=0.
best_human.evidence_state: Reconstructed from the formula and exact-checked over all 993 directions; the union has 8,641 points.
best_human.ai_provenance: This is the pre-AI traditional construction cited in the source.

best_public.provenance: AI-assisted multi-agent Station discovery. The paper discloses use of agents from multiple model families, and says GPT-5.5 operating outside the Station assisted formal verification. The formula is given in Section 6.1 and supported by a first-party verification notebook.
best_public.evidence_state: The published p=3 mod 4 formula gives 8,289 at p=31. The line witnesses were reconstructed and exactly checked here.

best_reproduced.verification_method: Generate the 993 explicit lines from the published formula; the checker reconstructs all 30,783 line points modulo 31 and counts the exact union.
best_reproduced.origin_type: local specialization and exact reproduction of a published AI-assisted construction

earlier_ai_result.source: A secondary public record list at https://zerothesis.com/challenges/kakeya-fp3?tab=brief attributes 8,290 at p=31 to the AlphaEvolve problem notebook. Georgiev et al., arXiv:2511.02864v3, Section 6.1 documents the related AI-assisted work but does not give a p=31 result table.
earlier_ai_result.provenance: The numerical attribution is secondary and was not located in the inspected primary paper or notebook. Treat it as an unreproduced reported value, not as a verified witness.
earlier_ai_result.note: The primary Station paper's 8,289 construction is smaller and is reproduced here.

parameters.construction: one affine line in each projective direction
parameters.objective: cardinality of the union of the represented lines

best_own_search.origin_type: Task-local construction from the simple seed; comparison assets were not read.

search_metadata.algorithm: seeded randomized greedy anchor replacement with exact marginal union counts

best_own_search.evidence_state: Strict replay and independent Sol review passed; see records.json.

lower_bound.source: Bukh and Chao, Sharp density bounds on the finite field Kakeya problem, 2021, Theorem 1; https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00074
lower_bound.status: rigorous finite lower bound, exact integer rounding of the published rational inequality

source_review.optimality_status: No exact finite minimum at p=31 was found in the reviewed sources. Bukh-Chao proves an asymptotically sharp leading constant, not a matching finite lower bound.
source_review.limitations: This is a bounded source review. A non-primary online table mentions 8,288 without an identified witness or primary derivation; it is not treated as a reliable record. The best directly sourced and reconstructed value is 8,289.
source_review.scope: The task concerns F_31^3 only. Results for other fields or dimensions are not compared as same-parameter records.

independent_quantity.method: projectivize every nonzero vector; repeated modular additions and dense finite-space bitmap
